Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/reference/configuration.md (lines 313-484 and 484-674). The file_changes ranges show only two changed regions: the "Last updated" date (line 3) and the `backend.enabled_models` row (line 201). Neither region falls in the supplied text units, so I reviewed the surrounding documentation for threat-model consistency only.

The patch excerpt describes a behavior change. A background `start` and a successful `switch` now save the model selection. A nonempty `enabled_models` acts as an operator filter, so coordinator `load_model`, `prefetch_model` and `desired_models` cannot load, download or advertise a model outside it (`ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift`, `operatorFilterAllows`). That tightens the coordinator-to-provider boundary (TB-002) and does not weaken it. I could not verify the implementation because it is not in the supplied evidence. The remaining uncertainty is whether the filter is enforced on every load path, including alias successors and Autopilot, but this documentation excerpt does not show it failing.

In the supplied text I found no new attack surface and no contradiction of the threat model. Items checked:
- Model cache location: cache changes require explicit operator selection; the environment import is one-time; paths are validated; `.artifact-writer-locks` are documented.
- SSD prefix cache: the `[cache]` table, `daily_write_gb` and the prefix-cache kill switches are consistent with T-041. The documented controls only narrow the TTL, encryption and memory safeguards.
- The remaining entries are documented environment variables for tuning and rollback. They are not forwarded to LaunchAgents unless listed, and they do not change attestation policy.

Follow-up for integration: confirm in code that `operatorFilterAllows` gates every coordinator-driven load path (TB-002, A-018), since the supplied documentation does not show this.
